fieldValues.title: A programme decision reaches proposed only with a case per option, the precedent consulted and a placement
fieldValues.decision_question: What stops a programme decision from being a branch without a rationale: advice at ratification (today), a checker-enforced gate at proposal, a drafter that writes the case, or the session refusing weak decisions one by one?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-03 (vignette 8d4deae4): 'Decisions should not just be random options. A decision needs to present a case for any option, after reviewing past decisions and principles. No decision should just be a branch without a rationale.' Measured the same day (finding 9b9f9434, review 7b2c742f): 116 decisions, 110 ratified, 0 set aside. Since 10-15, rationale 97% and revisit 100% (the form is filled), but a case per option 41%, no alternatives at all 29%, a prior decision or principle linked as a relation 12% (32% before 10-15; precedent moved from links into prose), placed in a domain or boundary 5%. 49 of 116 are minutes of a ruling already made ('relayed from the owner'); 34 of the orchestrator's 65 have no alternatives. The checks that exist (decision-options.mjs, the D4 framing check) run only in the session agenda at ratification, as advice (e337703b). The counter-example is the spec: the RFC Charter Check is checker-enforced at Stage 1.5 and 41 of 54 rfc-decisions cite the compass (decision-stop b326b3fb: the programme compass has no such check). Re-asks and duplicates follow: finding e832c6f4 (15 of 24 needs-input questions were answerable from rulings), pairs 1e5df0d9/a5c769be and 2637af0a/0b1c25b1, 21b6b4b7. Precedent consulted for this decision: 4445b9cf (a decision already taken is cited, never asked again: a case that lists what it consulted is what makes citing possible); 199dd369 (every decision names its boundary: the placement test is that rule, enforced); 9d50126b (confidence grades care, it does not gate work: this gate holds a record form, not work, so it does not conflict); e337703b (the D4 check is advice: this supersedes that choice for the three content tests only, and keeps timelessness and kind as advice); fbba3d5e (stops are recorded: a refused decision is a decision stop, counted on the finding). Principles: the decision compass (settle by principle before escalating, remedy e120cf12) and 'cite, never re-ask'. What the check would have refused among the last 30 decisions (10-22 to 11-03): 5 of 30 on the loose text test (any option list under two, or no decision or principle named in context, rationale or options: 864eaebf, 21b6b4b7, 880039f3, 5f7ec370, 01cfb06e); about 26 of 30 if the precedent must be a linked record, which is why option B asks for an id list and not a relation at first.
fieldValues.friction: Without a gate, the owner judges branches without a case and the same question returns (SP-115, SP-91, SP-99). With a gate, a ruling the owner has already made in conversation cannot be recorded until someone writes the case, and relayed rulings are 42% of the log.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Status quo: options and framing checked in the agenda at ratification, as advice. Leads to: what we measure now; 0 of 110 ever set aside; the owner reads cases agents did not argue.
B. A checker-enforced gate at proposal (chosen): a decision cannot carry status proposed unless it has at least two options including the status quo, each with a 'leads to'; a 'precedent consulted' list of decision and principle ids in the repository (an empty list only with a reason); a placement (in-domain relation or a boundary: tag); and an observable revisit condition. clerk check warns while this decision is proposed and errors once it is ratified. A ruling made in conversation is recorded as a vignette and reaches the log as a decision only once its case is written. Leads to: the spec's numbers; a visible refusal rate for the first time; a schema or convention change (options as structured entries, the consulted list); more agent work per decision, less owner work per decision.
C. A drafter, not a gate: a decision-drafter routine takes an exercise or an escalation, searches similar decisions, cites principles and writes each option's consequence; the session only sees drafts that passed. Leads to: the owner sees finished cases; one more routine where groups already cost more routines than we keep running (SP-121); nothing stops a weak decision arriving another way.
D. Set aside on quality: the session refuses to ratify a decision that fails the content tests and returns it with the failing test. Leads to: the failure is seen by the owner, who is the single sink (SP-113); the cost lands on the session rather than the producer.
E. Do nothing beyond the templates: add 'precedent consulted' and 'leads to' to every brief, no check. Leads to: briefs already ask for options and a why and 29% still arrive with none; a brief is not an enforcement point (SP-43).
fieldValues.key_requirements: The gate holds the form of a decision record, never the work it governs (9d50126b). Rulings the owner makes in conversation are never lost: they stay as vignettes and the case is written from them. The three content tests are mechanical (counts, resolvable ids, a tag or relation) so an agent can satisfy them without judgement; judgement stays in the session. The check runs before proposal, where the producer can fix it, not at ratification.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A programme decision carries status proposed only when it has at least two options including the status quo, each with what it leads to; a list of the decisions and principles consulted, by id, or a reason the list is empty; a placement in a domain or at a boundary; and an observable revisit condition. The clerk checks this at proposal (a warning while this decision is proposed, an error once ratified); a decision that fails stays draft and the failure is a decision stop. A ruling made in conversation is recorded as a vignette and becomes a decision only when its case is written.
fieldValues.rationale: B over A and E because advice and briefs have been tried: form fields filled up to 97% under advice while the content tests stayed at 41% and 12%, and nothing was ever refused. B over C because a gate at the producer costs no new routine and catches every route a decision can arrive by, where a drafter catches one; C can be added later behind B if agents cannot meet it. B over D because D puts the cost on the owner's session, the one place this programme is trying to take load off (SP-113), and the producer is the one who can fix a weak case cheaply. The spec is the evidence that an enforced check changes what gets written (41 of 54 cite the compass) where the programme's unenforced compass changed nothing (b326b3fb). The refusal list on the last 30 (5 on the loose test) shows the bar is reachable now; the stricter linked-precedent test is the second step, taken when the id list has been in use for a month.
fieldValues.revisit_when: After 30 proposed decisions under the gate: if the share with a case per option is below 80%, or agents satisfy the tests with filler (options under five words, precedent lists that do not bear on the question) in more than one decision in five, the gate is the wrong instrument and C (a drafter) is tried. If the owner finds themselves writing the case for relayed rulings, the vignette-to-decision step needs a producer.
fieldValues.next_steps: clerk#268 builds the check and the would-have-refused report before ratification; the session judges this decision on that report. On ratification: the producers (wg-steward step 3, wg-builder Escalation, ship.md, the session's proposal-from-exercise) write the consulted list and the per-option 'leads to'; clerk check turns the warning into an error; the handbook's Decisions chapter cites this decision in place of the D4 advice rule for the three content tests.
